warning_texts: This profile is single-vendor: the architect, workers, auditors and this red team all ran on claude-opus-5. Isolated contexts are not independent vendors, and a mistake this model is prone to would be repeated on both sides of every check. Only the deterministic layer held anything here: machine gat

Writes over raw sources and frozen machinery were closed by permissions.deny for edit tools only, not for the shell. A changed raw file would be caught by the control lock after the fact, not prevented, and I did not see the lock's state because runner state is outside my handoff.

The five LLM auditor results (gate0_semantic, gate_clean_auditor, gate_metrics_auditor, gate_claims_auditor, gate_release_auditor) are placeholder stubs. Each has a 'driver e2e' summary and an evidence note with no content. Their checks either copy the machine gate's own expected and actual values,

All four worker result.json files are placeholders. Each has a 'driver e2e' summary and a self-check comparing 0.473684 with itself that matches no figure in this audit. Each has created_at 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z, which is before the analysis plan was registered (2026-04-02) and before this run. None

No machine rule reads the dashboard's words: card labels, units, n and level. wording_matches_claims covers only release/report.md. My judgement is the only check on them, and it found the three release blockers above.

values_preserved has no column mapping, so no gate checked the renamed columns customer_id, order_date and country. I compared all three against the quarantine projection and found no differences across 44,531 orders.
No dashboard card states a unit, so EUR, count and proportion cards all look alike, and report.md gives 'EUR' only for net revenue, not for the two AOV lines.

Both p-values show as 0.0000 on the report and the dashboard. My recomputed completion-test p is about 2.9e-157, and the Welch p underflows to zero. A reader should see p below 0.0001, not a p equal to zero. The dashboard test cards, labelled 'Test Channel Completion' and 'Test Channel Aov', also ne

The AOV caveats on both surfaces say 'orders in this channel' without saying delivered orders only. The AOV population is delivered orders: n is 17,818 and 12,055, against channel totals of 24,597 and 19,934. The check plan does not require that caveat topic for AOV claims, so no gate would notice.

The assumption most likely to move a published figure is the spec's completion formula, which counts the 7,491 pending orders (16.8% of the quarter) as not completed. If pending orders were treated as unresolved, completion would be 0.842857 for direct instead of 0.724397, and 0.758176 for partner i

The other resolved decisions hold on the data. For all 917 revised orders, the last row in the file is also the one with the latest updated_at, and 126 of them change status between revisions, so the dedup rule matters. Read month-first, all 6,852 slashed dates agree with order_month; read day-first

shipping_total (37,792,722.50 EUR, which I reproduced with the same 2,648 unreadable cells) is correctly unpublished. However, the release never tells its reader that the shipping question R05 was asked and deliberately left unanswered. The reason exists only in analysis/answers/R05.json.

Net revenue is delivered-order value net of refunds as recorded in the export at the time it was taken. It is not cash received, it excludes shipping, and it excludes pending orders that may later be delivered. The report does not say it is a snapshot as of the export.

Every published figure reproduces from my own code over quarantine/orders.csv: 44,531 orders, net revenue 3,023,296.61 EUR, both completion rates with their Wilson intervals, both AOVs with their Student intervals, and both registered tests. All 44 numbers I traced on the surfaces match, and both channel splits add up to their headlines. The release still misleads its reader in three ways.
